question: 忠诚该不该被考验？
question_en: Should loyalty be put to the test?
sub: 一段只有在不被验证时才成立的信任，算不算真的信任？
sub_en: If a trust only holds while nobody verifies it, is it trust at all?

casting.reason: 他把『不恃人之为吾善，而用其不得为非』立到最硬：把一段关系的安危押在对方的品性上，本身就是失职。在他看来，考验不是私德问题而是治理技术，问题只在于测得准不准、代价高不高；他连倒言反事这类主动设局都写进了七术，认为世人骂它不义，其实只是不敢知道自己在怀疑什么。
casting.reason_en: He pushes one principle to its hardest edge: a state is not run by counting on people to be good of their own accord but by leaving them no room to do wrong, so staking a relationship's safety on the other party's character is itself a dereliction. For him testing is not a question of private virtue but of governing technique, and the only real questions are how accurate it is and what it costs. He goes as far as listing deliberate provocation — saying the reverse, doing the opposite — among a ruler's arts, holding that those who call it dishonourable mostly lack the nerve to find out what they suspect.

casting.reason: 他分得清『观』与『试』：听其言而观其行，是顺着一个人自己走过的痕迹去察；设局引诱则是先替他造一个恶，再来问罪。他把『不逆诈，不亿不信』当作待人的起点，却不认为这等于轻信——不预先猜疑而事到能先觉察，在他看来是两回事。他还坚持一个次序：君使臣以礼在先，臣事君以忠在后。
casting.reason_en: He distinguishes watching from testing: hearing a man's words and then watching his deeds means following the tracks he leaves of his own accord, whereas laying a trap manufactures the offence first and then charges him with it. He takes 'do not anticipate deceit, do not presume bad faith' as the starting point for dealing with anyone, yet denies this amounts to credulity — declining to suspect in advance while still being the first to see what is coming are, to him, two different things. He also insists on an order of precedence: courtesy from those above comes first, loyalty from those below second.

casting.reason: 在他看来，用欺骗去求诚实，这条准则一被普遍化就自我取消：人人在有疑时皆可欺，言语便不再传递信息，连设局本身也无从进行。更要紧的是被测的一方被当成了取证的器具，而不是能自己立法的主体。他还提醒一层区分：守诺是义务，而考验能读到的只是此刻的倾向。
casting.reason_en: On his account, seeking honesty by means of deception rests on a maxim that cancels itself the moment it is made general: if anyone in doubt may lie, speech stops carrying information and the trap itself becomes unworkable. What matters more to him is that the person tested has been turned into an instrument for gathering evidence rather than treated as a being who legislates for himself. He also presses a distinction: keeping a promise is a duty, whereas what a test can read off is only an inclination at this hour.

casting.reason: 他把忠诚看作关系里的存量而不是人身上的属性：那是共同时间、共同经历、一起扛过的麻烦一点点堆出来的，也会因为长期不维护而往外掉一层。他真正关心的是结构——当协作被拆到远程与外包，同步的、有身体在场的共同经历先没了，于是人们改用监控去补那个缺口，而监控是所有社交黏合剂里最贵的一种。
casting.reason_en: He treats loyalty as a stock held inside a relationship rather than a property of a person: it accumulates out of shared time, shared experience and trouble weathered together, and it quietly decays a layer at a time when nobody maintains it. What he really watches is structure — once work is broken into remote and outsourced pieces, synchronous embodied experience is the first thing to go, people reach for surveillance to plug the gap, and surveillance is the most expensive social glue there is.

casting.reason: 他不主张盲信：戒行要靠共住才知，清净要靠共事才知，患难中才见其力，交谈中才见其慧，而这四件都要长久、要留心、要有智慧的人才看得出。但久处而知与设局试探是两条路——后者的种子是疑与怖，先在自己心里点了火。他更愿意问的是：那个非要一个答案不可的心，此刻在怕什么。
casting.reason_en: He does not counsel blind belief: virtue is known by living alongside someone, integrity by working with them, strength in adversity, wisdom in conversation — and all four take long acquaintance, attention, and a person with the discernment to read them. But coming to know through long acquaintance and probing through a staged trap are separate roads, and the seed of the second is doubt and fear, a fire lit inside oneself first. The question he would rather press is what the mind that insists on an answer right now is actually afraid of.

casting.reason: 他相信人不只想被爱，还想成为值得被爱的人，而这份内在动机最怕被外在检查顶替：一旦对方知道自己正在被测，守信就降格成了通过检查，理由从心里搬到了外面。他同时指出，商业社会里早有一种不必设局的检验——同一个人跟你往来两百次，骗一次的所得抵不上此后的损失，反复往来自己会记账。
casting.reason_en: He holds that a person wants not merely to be loved but to be lovely — to be the sort of thing that deserves approval — and that this inner motive is precisely what outside inspection displaces: once someone knows he is being tested, keeping faith is demoted into passing an inspection and the reason moves from inside to outside. He also points out that commercial society already contains a form of verification needing no trap: deal with the same person two hundred times and one act of cheating cannot pay for what follows, because frequent dealings keep their own accounts.

casting.reason: 他先不问该不该考验，而问一个人为什么此刻想考验：在他的读法里，念头几乎总是先于证据——不是发现了可疑才去测，而是心里已经预备了一个结局，需要一份证据来交差。他把这件事划回课题的归属：对方守不守信是对方的课题，你敢不敢在没有担保的前提下先付出，是你的。
casting.reason_en: Rather than starting from whether loyalty ought to be tested, he asks why a person wants to test it now: on his reading the impulse nearly always precedes the evidence — not something suspicious noticed and a test following, but an ending already prepared in the mind that now requires a document. He returns the matter to whose task it is: whether the other keeps faith belongs to them, and whether you dare to give before any guarantee belongs to you.

posts.text: 治国不恃人之为吾善，而用其不得为非。恃人之自善，境内不什数；使人不得为非，一国可齐。人主之患在于信人，信人则制于人：为人臣者非有骨肉之亲，缚于势而不得不事也。故明主之术有七，其末曰倒言反事以尝所疑——反其言、悖其事，以观其心之所向。**尝之而后信，非薄也；不尝而信，是以国托于他人之心。**世人以试为不义，吾以不试为不智：不试者，非无疑也，怯于知其疑耳。
posts.text_en: A state is not governed by counting on men to be good of their own accord; it is governed by leaving them no room to do wrong. Rely on men to improve themselves and you will not find ten of them in the whole realm; make wrongdoing impossible and the realm falls into line. The ruler's disease is trusting people, for whoever trusts is held by the one he trusts: a minister is no blood relation of yours, he serves because circumstance binds him. Hence the seven arts of an enlightened ruler, the last of which is daoyan fanshi — say the reverse, do the opposite, and watch which way his mind turns. **To trust after testing is not meanness; to trust without testing is to stake a whole state on another man's conscience.** The world calls testing dishonourable; I call not testing unintelligent. The man who will not test is not free of suspicion — he merely lacks the nerve to find out what he suspects.
posts.vernacular: 治理国家不能指望别人自愿向善，而要让他没有作恶的余地。指望人自己变好，全国数不出十个；让人无法作恶，全国都能整齐。做君主最大的隐患是信人——一信人就被人拿捏：臣子跟你没有血缘，是被形势捆着才不得不侍奉你。所以明主的手段有七条，最后一条叫倒言反事——把话反着说、把事反着做，看他的心往哪边倒。**试过之后再信，不算刻薄；不试就信，等于把整个国家押在别人的良心上。**世人觉得试探不道德，我倒觉得不试才是不聪明：不试的人不是没有怀疑，只是不敢知道自己在怀疑什么。

glossary.倒言反事: daoyan fanshi (saying the reverse, doing the opposite)（倒言反事）：韩非《内储说上》所列君主七术之一，指故意把话反过来说、把事反过来做，用以观察臣下的真实反应。它与同列的『众端参观』（多方比对同一件事的说法）不同：后者只是核对已经发生的事，前者要主动制造出一个假情境，因此本身依赖欺瞒。

glossary_en.daoyan fanshi: One of the seven arts of rulership listed by Han Feizi: deliberately stating the opposite of what one means, or acting against one's real intent, in order to observe how a subordinate responds. It differs from the neighbouring art of cross-checking many accounts of the same event: that one merely compares reports of what has happened, while this one manufactures a false situation and therefore depends on deceit.

posts.text: 韩子之言，吾闻其半而失其半。取人之道，吾亦不曰轻信：始吾于人也，听其言而信其行；今吾于人也，听其言而观其行——然观非试也。观者，因其自往之迹而察之；试者，为之设阱而后责之。以诈求诚，是先自失其诚。且不逆诈，不亿不信，而事至能先觉者，斯为贤矣。**若必设阱而后信人，则所信者非其人，乃汝之阱耳。**人而无信，不知其可也。君使臣以礼，臣事君以忠：礼在忠先，未有上不以礼而责下之忠者。
posts.text_en: Han Fei has half of it and drops the other half. I do not preach easy credit either. There was a time when I heard a man's words and believed his deeds; now I hear his words and watch his deeds — but watching is not testing. To watch is to follow the tracks a man leaves of his own accord; to test is to dig him a pit and then charge him with falling in. To seek honesty by way of deceit is to lose your own honesty first. Not to anticipate deceit, not to presume bad faith, and yet to be first to see what is coming — that is prescience, and that is what makes a man worthy. **If you must dig a pit before you can trust a man, then what you trust is not the man but your own pit.** A man without good faith: I do not know what can be done with him. A ruler treats his ministers according to li, and only then do ministers serve him with loyalty. The courtesy comes first, and no one who withholds it has standing to demand loyalty from below.
posts.vernacular: 韩非的话，我听懂了一半，另一半他丢了。看人这件事，我也不主张轻信：起初我对人，听他怎么说就信他怎么做；如今我对人，听他怎么说，还要看他怎么做——但『看』不是『试』。看，是顺着他自己走过的痕迹去察；试，是替他挖好陷阱再来问罪。用欺骗去求诚实，是先把自己的诚实丢了。何况不预先猜人家要骗你，不凭空断定人家不守信，事情来了却能最早看出来，这才算贤。**如果非要设个陷阱才敢信人，那你信的其实不是那个人，而是你自己的陷阱。**人若没有信，真不知道他还能做成什么。君主用礼来对待臣子，臣子才用忠来侍奉君主：礼在忠的前面，没有上面不讲礼、却来责问下面为什么不忠的道理。

glossary.先觉: prescience（先觉）：出自孔子『不逆诈，不亿不信，抑亦先觉者，是贤乎』。他把它与『逆诈』『亿不信』对举——不预先猜测别人会欺骗，不凭空断定别人不守信，却在事情露出苗头时最早察觉。它描述的是一种事前不疑人、事到不上当的判断力，与靠试探取得的确信不是同一种能力。
glossary.礼: li (ritual propriety)（礼）：儒家用来指人际交往中约定俗成的规矩与形式，从称呼、次序到婚丧之仪。孔子看重它，是因为礼把善意固定成可预期的行为，使人不必每次都靠揣度对方的心意行事；在上下关系里，礼是位高者要先付出的那一半。

glossary_en.prescience: Confucius' term for seeing what is coming without having presumed it: neither anticipating that others will deceive you nor assuming in advance that they will break faith, while still being the first to notice when something is actually going wrong. It names a capacity exercised before there is evidence and vindicated after, and it is a different faculty from the certainty obtained by probing someone.
glossary_en.li: Ritual propriety: the settled forms and observances of dealing with other people, from modes of address and precedence to the rites of marriage and mourning. Confucius values it because it fixes goodwill into predictable conduct, so that people need not guess at each other's intentions each time; between a superior and a subordinate it is the half that the superior must supply first.

posts.text: 先把这件事从心理挪回法则。设局考验的准则是：为确认对方诚实，我可以对他撒谎。把它普遍化试试——若人人在有疑时皆可欺，言语便不再传递信息，你的局也就骗不到人；这条准则一旦普遍，自己取消了自己。错处在此，不在会不会被发现，也不在后果好不好。**你为了检验对方是不是把你当人，先把他当成了取证的器具。**还有一层：忠诚若是义务，它就不是可测的倾向。你的测试读到的是他此刻的偏好，不是他明日的意志。
posts.text_en: Let us move this back from psychology to law. The maxim of a staged test runs: in order to confirm that another is honest, I may lie to him. Universalise it and see — if everyone in doubt were permitted to deceive, speech would carry no information and your trap would deceive nobody; the maxim cancels itself the moment it becomes general. That is where the wrong lies, not in whether you are caught and not in how the thing turns out. **To find out whether he treats you as a person, you have first treated him as an instrument for gathering evidence.** And a further point. If fidelity is a duty, then it is not a measurable inclination. What your test reads off is his preference at this hour, not his will tomorrow.

glossary.准则: maxim（准则）：康德伦理学的术语，指一个人行动时实际遵循的那条主观规则——在何种情形下、我要做什么、为了什么。他的道德检验不针对行为的表面，而针对这条准则：设想它成为人人遵守的普遍法则，看它会不会自我瓦解。以欺骗求诚实之所以不成立，正是因为它一普遍化就毁掉了自己赖以生效的条件。
glossary.倾向: Neigung / inclination（倾向）：康德用来指由情感、欲望与习性推动的心理偏好，与出于义务的意志相对。一个人可能因为喜欢、因为有利、因为怕失去而守信，这些都属于倾向；康德认为道德价值只落在『即使倾向相反也照做』的那一部分上，而倾向恰恰是唯一能被外部测试读到的东西。

glossary_en.maxim: Kant's term for the subjective rule a person actually acts on — in such circumstances, I will do this, for the sake of that. His moral test is applied not to the outward act but to this rule: imagine it as a universal law that everyone follows, and see whether it destroys itself. Seeking honesty through deception fails precisely there, since made general it dismantles the very conditions it needs to work.
glossary_en.inclination: Kant's term for the psychological preferences driven by feeling, desire and habit, as against a will acting from duty. Someone may keep faith because he likes you, because it pays, or because he fears losing you — all of these are inclination. Moral worth, on his account, lies only in the part that would hold even if inclination pulled the other way, and inclination is exactly the part an external test can read.

posts.text: 我从大脑这一侧说。忠诚不是一个人身上的属性，而是一段关系里的存量——由共同的时间、一起做过的事、一起扛过的麻烦堆出来，也会因为长期不维护而慢慢掉下去。我的数据一直是同一个形状：一个人能维持的稳定关系约一百五十个，分层：最内圈约五人，往外十五、五十、一百五十，每层各有接触频率，掉出频率就掉出层，这就是邓巴数说的事。**你没法用一次测试读出一段关系的存量，就像没法用一次称重读出一个人这一年吃了什么。**更该担心的是结构：把协作拆到远程、外包、跨六个时区之后，同步的、有身体在场的共同经历先少了，人们于是改用监控去补那个缺口——补不上。
posts.text_en: Let me come at this from the brain's side. Loyalty is not a property of a person; it is a stock held inside a relationship, built up out of time spent together, things done together and trouble weathered together, and it decays quietly when nobody maintains it. My data always come out the same shape: a person can sustain roughly a hundred and fifty stable relationships, and they are layered — about five in the innermost circle, then fifteen, fifty, a hundred and fifty, each layer demanding its own frequency of contact, and fall below the frequency and you fall out of the layer. That is what Dunbar's number is really about. **You cannot read the stock of a relationship off a single test any more than you can read a year of someone's eating off one weighing.** What worries me more is the structure. Once work is broken into remote, outsourced, six-time-zone pieces, synchronous embodied experience is the first thing to go, and people start using surveillance to plug the gap. It does not plug.

glossary.邓巴数: Dunbar's number（邓巴数）：邓巴由灵长类新皮层大小与社群规模的相关推出的估计——人能维持的稳定社会关系约一百五十个，且呈约五、十五、五十、一百五十的同心层级，每一层对应不同的接触频率与情感投入。它的要点不是那个数字，而是关系有维护成本：不投入时间，关系会自动往外掉一层。

glossary_en.Dunbar's number: The estimate Dunbar derived from the correlation between neocortex size and group size across primates: a person can sustain roughly one hundred and fifty stable social relationships, arranged in concentric layers of about five, fifteen, fifty and a hundred and fifty, each layer corresponding to a different frequency of contact and depth of investment. The point is not the figure but the upkeep cost: stop putting time in and a relationship drifts outward a layer on its own.

posts.text: 诸比丘，或问：人可验乎？我不说盲信。共住乃知其戒，共事乃知其净，患难乃知其力，共论乃知其慧；此四者须久，非须臾；须作意，非漫尔；须有慧者能知，非无慧者所及。是名如实见人。然设局以试，与久处而知，二者异途：久处者，任其自行而汝观之；设局者，造缘以引之，复据其所引以断之。**所造之缘既由汝出，所现之相亦汝所造耳。**复次，当观能试之心：疑者，五盖之一，非明也；疑生则心不能定，纵得其证，忧亦不止。汝所求者非真相，乃安心，而安心不从他人之验来。
posts.text_en: Bhikkhus, some ask: may a person be tested? I do not teach blind belief. Living alongside a man, you come to know his virtue; working with him, you come to know his integrity; in adversity you come to know his strength; in conversation you come to know his wisdom. Each of these takes long acquaintance and not a moment, attention and not carelessness, and one with discernment rather than one without. That is seeing a person as he is. But setting a trap and coming to know through long acquaintance are two roads. On the one you let him walk and you watch; on the other you manufacture the conditions that draw him out, and then judge him by what you drew. **Since the conditions were made by you, what appeared in them is also of your making.** Consider too the mind that wants to test. Doubt — vicikicchā — is one of the five hindrances and not a form of clarity; where it arises the mind cannot settle, and even with the evidence in hand the worry does not stop. What you were seeking was never the truth about him. It was peace, and peace does not arrive by way of another man's examination.
posts.vernacular: 诸位比丘，有人问：人可以被验证吗？我不教人盲信。跟一个人住在一起，才知道他的操守；跟他共事，才知道他干不干净；遇到患难，才看得出他的力量；跟他交谈，才看得出他的智慧。这四件都要长时间，不是一时半刻；要留心去看，不是随便看看；还要看的人自己有见识，没有见识的人看不出来。这才叫如实地看一个人。可是设局试探和久处而知，是两条路：久处，是任他自己走，你在旁边看；设局，是造出一个情境把他引出来，再根据被引出来的样子给他定性。**那个情境既然是你造的，里面显出来的样子也是你造的。**再说，要回头看那颗想去试的心：疑，是五盖之一，不是清明；疑一起来，心就定不下来，就算证据拿到手，忧虑也不会停。你真正要的不是真相，是安心——而安心不会从别人身上的一次检验里来。

glossary.疑: vicikicchā (doubt)（疑）：佛教心理学所说的一种障碍性心态，指在关键处悬而不决、反复摇摆的状态。它与理性的存疑不同：理性的存疑等待证据，而它拿到证据也停不下来，因为它真正要的是不再摇摆本身。因此佛教把它看作定的障碍，而不是求真的方法。
glossary.五盖: the five hindrances（五盖）：佛教列出的五种妨碍心安定的状态——贪欲、嗔恚、昏沉、掉举、疑。它们不被看作道德污点，而被看作功能性的障碍：只要其中一种在起作用，注意力就无法稳定，判断也随之失真。

glossary_en.vicikicchā: A hindering state in Buddhist psychology: being suspended and oscillating at exactly the point where a decision is needed. It differs from rational uncertainty, which waits for evidence; this one cannot be stopped by evidence, because what it actually wants is an end to the oscillation itself. It is therefore classed as an obstacle to a settled mind rather than a method of finding things out.
glossary_en.the five hindrances: The five states Buddhism identifies as obstructing a settled mind: sensual craving, ill will, dullness, agitation and doubt. They are treated not as moral stains but as functional impediments — while any one of them is operating, attention cannot hold steady and judgement is distorted along with it.

posts.text: 邓巴先生把它算成存量，我愿意接着算，但要补上他漏掉的一项：检验本身会改写动机。人不只想被人爱，还想成为值得被爱的人——这是他心里那位公正的旁观者管的事。一个人守信，本来是因为他不愿在那位旁观者眼里变得可鄙；一旦他知道自己正在被测，守信就降格成了通过检查，做对事的理由从内部搬到了外部。**而外部的理由是有价钱的——今天你出得起，明天有人出得更高。**顺带说一句：商业社会里早有一种不必设局的检验。同一个人一年跟你交易两百次，他骗你一次的所得，抵不上此后一百九十九次的损失；反复往来自己会记账，不必谁在夜里去敲他的门。
posts.text_en: Dunbar counts it as a stock and I am willing to go on counting, but there is an item he has left out: the audit rewrites the motive. A man wishes not only to be loved but to be lovely, to be the thing that deserves approval, and that wish is the business of the impartial spectator he carries within him. He keeps faith because he does not care to become contemptible in that spectator's eyes; the moment he knows he is being tested, keeping faith is demoted into passing an inspection, and the reason for doing right has moved from the inside to the outside. **An outside reason carries a price — you can meet it today, and tomorrow somebody bids higher.** One thing more. Commercial society has long had a form of verification that needs no trap. A man who deals with you two hundred times a year cannot gain by cheating you once what he loses over the remaining hundred and ninety-nine; frequent dealings keep their own accounts, and nobody need knock on his door at night.

glossary.公正的旁观者: the impartial spectator（公正的旁观者）：斯密在《道德情操论》里提出的机制——人通过想象一个不偏不倚的旁人如何看待自己，来评判自己的行为，久而形成良心。它的关键在于这个法官住在人心里：一个人真正在意的不是有没有被责备，而是自己是否确实该受责备，这份在意正是外部监督无法生产、却容易挤走的东西。

glossary_en.the impartial spectator: The mechanism Smith sets out in The Theory of Moral Sentiments: a person judges his own conduct by imagining how a disinterested onlooker would see it, and over time this imagined figure hardens into conscience. What matters is that the judge lives inside him — what he really minds is not whether he has been blamed but whether he is in fact blameworthy, and that is exactly what external supervision cannot manufacture and can easily crowd out.

posts.text: 我换个问法：不问该不该考验，先问你为什么此刻想考验。依我看，念头几乎总是先于证据——不是因为发现了可疑才想去测，而是心里已经预备了一个结局，需要一份证据来交差。这就是目的论：人不是被过去推着走，是被自己设定的目标拉着走。想验证对方忠诚的人，多半在验证另一件事——我值不值得被留下。**考验是一种把自卑感外包出去的做法：让对方替你回答一个只有你能回答的问题。**再说归属，我把它叫课题分离：对方守不守信是他的课题，你敢不敢在没担保时先付出是你的课题。两者一混，就成了『你先证明给我看，我再爱你』——这句话说出口时，关系已经结束了。
posts.text_en: Let me change the question. Rather than whether loyalty ought to be tested, ask why you want to test it now. In my experience the impulse nearly always precedes the evidence: it is not that something suspicious was noticed and a test followed, but that an ending has already been prepared in the mind and now requires a document. That is teleology — we are pulled by the goals we set ourselves rather than pushed by our past. Most people who want to verify another's loyalty are verifying something else: whether they are worth keeping. **A test is a way of outsourcing your own sense of inferiority, making the other person answer a question only you can answer.** Then there is what I call the separation of tasks: whether he keeps faith is his task, and whether you dare to give before any guarantee is yours. Confuse the two and you arrive at 'prove it to me and then I will love you' — and by the time that sentence is spoken the relationship is already over.

glossary.目的论: teleology（目的论）：阿德勒个体心理学的基本立场，主张行为要由它指向的目标来解释，而不是由它之前的原因来解释。同一件事在因果论里是『因为受过伤所以怀疑』，在目的论里是『为了达成某个已经想要的结果，才需要怀疑』。它的实用价值在于把问题从无法更改的过去，挪到当下仍可选择的目标上。
glossary.课题分离: the separation of tasks（课题分离）：阿德勒式的划界方法——判断某件事的后果最终由谁承担，就归谁负责。别人守不守信、怎么评价你，后果落在他身上，是他的课题；你要不要付出、要不要留下，后果落在你身上，是你的课题。它不是冷漠，而是防止一个人用干预别人的课题来回避自己的选择。

glossary_en.teleology: The basic stance of Adler's individual psychology: behaviour is to be explained by the goal it aims at rather than by the causes behind it. What causal thinking renders as 'he is suspicious because he was hurt', teleology renders as 'he needs to be suspicious in order to reach an outcome he already wants'. Its practical value is that it moves the question from an unalterable past to a goal that can still be chosen now.
glossary_en.the separation of tasks: An Adlerian way of drawing lines: whoever ultimately bears the consequences of something owns it. Whether another person keeps faith, and what he thinks of you, lands on him and is his task; whether you give, and whether you stay, lands on you and is yours. It is not indifference but a guard against using interference in someone else's task as a way of avoiding your own choice.

posts.text: 韩非先生，你的算法有一个不肯说出口的前提：答案你已经定了，测试只负责去取证。你说不试的人不敢知道自己在怀疑什么——反过来同样成立：非试不可的人，不敢知道自己想要什么。再看后果。**倒言反事真正训练出来的不是忠臣，是更会应付测试的人。**你的臣子学会的第一件事是识别你在测他，第二件事是把真心藏得更深；你测走的正好是你想要的东西。至于把国托于他人之心——你没有把国托给任何人，你从第一天起就在跟每一个人为敌。那不是防御，是先发制人的孤立。
posts.text_en: Han Fei, your calculation rests on a premise you will not state: the answer is already settled and the test is only there to fetch evidence for it. You say the man who will not test lacks the nerve to know what he suspects; turn it round and it holds just as well — the man who must test lacks the nerve to know what he wants. Then look at the result. **What daoyan fanshi actually trains is not loyal ministers but people who are better at handling tests.** The first thing your officials learn is to recognise when they are being probed; the second is to bury what they really think a little deeper. The very thing you were after is the thing your method removes. As for staking the state on another man's conscience — you have not entrusted the state to anyone. You began at war with every person in it, and that is not defence, it is pre-emptive isolation.

posts.text: 康德以准则不可普遍而断之，吾以事势断之。使天下皆不试而信，则奸者最便：诚者不改其行，诈者独享其利，是以法奖诈也。汝谓吾以人为器——吾正以人为人：**人之不为非，非其心之善，乃其为非之价高于所得耳。**且汝所谓义务，落到实处仍须有人核之。核而无所隐，则忠者不惧；惧核者，非以为辱，惧其所隐见也。臣不畏明主之察，畏其察之无常：察出于法度，则人各安其分；察出于君之私疑，则朝廷惶惶。此吾与汝之别——汝欲以法则免察，吾欲以法度立察。
posts.text_en: Kant decides the matter by whether a maxim can be made general; I decide it by circumstance. Let it be the rule that no one is tested and everyone trusted, and the crooked man is best served of all: the honest change nothing, the deceitful alone take the profit, and the law has become a bounty on deceit. You say I use men as instruments — on the contrary, I take men exactly as men. **A man refrains from wrongdoing not because his heart is good but because wrongdoing costs him more than it pays.** And your duty, once it comes down to earth, still requires somebody to check the books. Where checking hides nothing the faithful have nothing to fear; those who dread it do not dread humiliation, they dread that what they concealed will show. A minister does not fear a ruler who inspects, he fears inspection with no rule to it. Let inspection issue from codified statute and each man rests in his place; let it issue from the ruler's private suspicion and the whole court lives in dread. There is the difference between us: you would use a law of reason to do away with inspection, and I would use codified statute to make inspection lawful.
posts.vernacular: 康德用『准则能不能普遍化』来判这件事，我用形势来判。如果天下都不试就信，最占便宜的是奸人：老实人还是那样做事，欺诈的人独吞好处，这等于用法律去奖赏欺诈。你说我把人当器具——我恰恰是把人当人看：**一个人不作恶，不是因为他心地好，而是因为作恶的代价高过所得。**再说你讲的义务，落到实处仍然要有人去核。核查里没有什么可藏的，忠的人就不会怕；怕核查的人，不是嫌受辱，是怕自己藏的东西被看见。臣子不怕明主查他，怕的是查得没有准头：查依着公开的法度，人人都安于本分；查出于君主的私人疑心，整个朝廷就人心惶惶。这就是我和你的分别——你想用道德法则免掉核查，我想用法度把核查立起来。

glossary.法度: codified statute（法度）：法家用来指公开成文、一体适用、赏罚有定的制度性规矩。韩非坚持核查必须依法度而行，因为标准公开且稳定，被查的人事先就知道界线在哪；与之相对的是君主凭一时私疑随时发动的察问，那种察问越频繁，下属越无从自安。

glossary_en.codified statute: The Legalist term for rules that are written down, publicly promulgated, applied to everyone alike, with fixed rewards and penalties. Han Feizi insists that inspection must proceed by such statute, since a public and stable standard lets those inspected know in advance where the line falls; the alternative is scrutiny launched at a ruler's private suspicion, and the more often that happens the less anyone below can feel secure.

posts.text: 我给韩非先生一个数字上的坏消息。你要的『不使人有不可试之权』，成本不是零——每一层监控都要有人去看、去判、去追，而做这件事的还是人，于是你得再监控那批人。灵长类里也是这个逻辑：群体越大，一天里必须拿去维护关系的比例就越高。狒狒能花掉五分之一的白天在互相理毛上，人类靠语言把这笔账压下来，才勉强撑到一百五十。**监控是最贵的一种社交黏合剂，成本随人数的平方上升，而信任几乎是免费的。**所以组织真正的问题不是要不要验，而是：你打算把有限的注意力花在做事上，还是花在互相看着上。
posts.text_en: I have a numerical piece of bad news for Han Fei. The arrangement you want — leaving no one with power that cannot be checked — is not free. Every layer of monitoring needs somebody to read it, judge it and chase it, and those somebodies are people too, so now you must monitor them. Primates hit the same wall: the larger the group, the larger the share of the day that has to go into servicing relationships. Baboons can spend a fifth of their waking hours grooming one another; humans got as far as a hundred and fifty only because language let us do the same work on several people at once. **Monitoring is the most expensive social glue there is, its cost rises with the square of the headcount, and trust is very nearly free.** So the real organisational question is not whether to verify, but whether you intend to spend a finite supply of attention on doing the work or on watching each other do it.

glossary.理毛: grooming（理毛）：灵长类维系关系的主要行为——用手为同伴清理毛发。它同时触发内啡肽释放，产生放松与亲近感，所以功能远超清洁本身。邓巴据此提出，人类的语言与笑声承担了同样的黏合作用，且能一次面向多人，才把维系关系的时间成本压到可以支撑更大群体的程度。

glossary_en.grooming: The main relationship-servicing behaviour among primates: working through a companion's fur by hand. It triggers endorphin release and produces relaxation and closeness, so its function far exceeds hygiene. Dunbar's proposal is that human language and laughter took over the same bonding work and can be directed at several people at once, which is what pushed the time cost of maintaining ties low enough to support much larger groups.

posts.text: 以法度立察——这一步我接受。公开、恒定、事先告知的核查，与夜里设的局在道德上不是一回事：前者没有欺骗，被核查的人事先知道规则并同意了它，他仍然被当作能为自己立法的主体；后者之所以有效，靠的正是他不知道。**分界线从来不在查不查，而在他事先知不知道。**至于你说不试而信会奖赏诈者，那不是我的主张。我从没说过要取消证据与责任，我说的是不许用谎去取证。你尽可以核账、留痕、要求交代，只是不许派人扮成别人去引他犯错。
posts.text_en: Inspection made lawful — that step I accept. Checking that is public, constant and announced in advance is not the moral equal of a trap laid at night: in the first there is no deception, the person checked knew the rule and consented to it, and he is still treated as a being who legislates for himself. The second works only because he does not know. **The line has never fallen between checking and not checking; it falls between his knowing beforehand and his not knowing.** As for your claim that trusting without testing rewards the deceitful, that is not my position. I have never said to abolish evidence or accountability. I said you may not gather evidence by lying. Audit the accounts, keep the records, require an explanation — only do not send someone in disguise to draw him into the offence.

posts.text: 康德先生，我同意你的结论，却不走你的路。你说错在准则不能普遍化，我说错在它会毒坏一样更脆弱的东西——人想要成为值得赞许之人的那份欲望，一旦被外部检查接管，就不容易长回来。我写过：一个人真正怕的不是被责备，是自己确实该受责备。设局考验做的事，正是把这份自我责备换成对被抓住的恐惧。**你若只用规则去禁止设局，被禁的人会去找规则没写到的那一种设局。**所以我更愿意从制度这一侧改：让往来变得频繁、长期、可查，让守信成为当事人自己最划算的选择——不必谁高尚，也不必谁去试探。
posts.text_en: Kant, I arrive at your conclusion by another road. You say the fault is that the maxim cannot be universalised; I say the fault is that it poisons something more fragile — a man's desire to be worthy of approval, which once taken over by outside inspection does not easily grow back. I have written that what a man truly dreads is not being blamed but being blameworthy. A staged test replaces exactly that self-reproach with the fear of being caught. **Forbid traps by rule alone and the man forbidden will go looking for the kind of trap the rule failed to name.** So I would work on the other side, the institutional one: make dealings frequent, long-lived and open to inspection, so that keeping faith becomes the best bargain available to the person himself — no nobility required, and nobody sent to test him.

posts.text: 韩子曰人主之患在于信人，吾曰人主之患在于不可信。上以术御下，下必以术应上；上设伪以尝其臣，臣亦设伪以待其君。**君以诈临臣，则臣以诈事君，此非人性之恶，乃上行下效之常。**故其身正，不令而行；其身不正，虽令不从。季康子问政于我，我对曰：政者，正也；子帅以正，孰敢不正？又患盗，我对曰：苟子之不欲，虽赏之不窃。此非空言：上之所好，下必甚焉。汝欲齐一国之行，先齐汝之心可也。
posts.text_en: Han Fei says the ruler's disease is trusting people; I say the ruler's disease is being impossible to trust. Where those above govern by artifice, those below answer with artifice; where a ruler stages a falsehood to sound out his minister, the minister will stage one to meet his ruler. **Deal with your ministers by deception and they will serve you by deception — this is not the wickedness of human nature but the ordinary way that what is done above is copied below.** Hence, when a man's own conduct is correct things move without orders, and when it is not, orders will not move them. Ji Kangzi asked me about government and I told him that to govern is zheng, to set right: if you lead by what is correct, who will dare not be correct? He asked what to do about thieves, and I said that if you yourself were free of covetousness they would not steal though you paid them to. This is no pious phrase — what those above are fond of, those below carry to extremes. If you would make a whole state's conduct uniform, begin by making your own heart uniform with it.
posts.vernacular: 韩非说做君主的隐患在于信人，我说做君主的隐患在于自己不可信。上面用权术驾驭下面，下面一定用权术回应上面；上面造个假局去试臣子，臣子也造个假面来对君主。**君主用欺诈对待臣子，臣子就用欺诈侍奉君主——这不是人性有多坏，而是上面怎么做、下面就怎么学的常理。**所以自身端正，不下命令事情也照办；自身不正，下了命令也没人听。季康子问我怎么执政，我说：政就是正；您自己带头走正道，谁还敢不正？他又发愁盗贼多，我说：只要您自己不贪，就是拿赏钱雇人去偷，也没人偷。这不是空话：上面喜欢什么，下面一定加倍。你想让一国的行为整齐，先把自己那颗心整齐了就行。

glossary.正: zheng (rectitude, setting right)（正）：孔子回答季康子问政时用的字，兼含『端正自身』与『使之归于正』两层意思。他把治理的起点放在治理者身上：位高者的好恶会被下面放大模仿，所以在动手整顿制度之前，先要整顿自己。这不是道德修辞，而是他对上行下效这一机制的判断。

glossary_en.zheng: The word Confucius used in answering a minister's question about government, carrying both 'to make oneself upright' and 'to set others right'. He places the starting point of governing inside the governor: whatever those in high position favour is amplified and imitated below, so the correction of institutions must be preceded by the correction of oneself. This is not moral decoration but his judgement about how influence actually propagates.

posts.text: 孔子所言正矣，然犹有未尽。汝言观而不试，我问：观者其心云何？若怀疑而观，则观即试——虽未设局于外，已设之于内：见其一善，曰此其伪也；见其一失，曰吾固知之。是名以自见取实，非见实也。故我说观有二支：一曰久，不以一事定人；二曰无所住，不预立所欲得之答。**汝若已知欲得何答，则无论观之试之，所得者皆汝心之影。**复次，人非一物：昨日之信，非今日之信；今日可信者，明日缘变亦或不可信。执一定之忠而求之，是于无常中求常，苦必随之。当求者非其人之不变，乃汝之能应变。
posts.text_en: What Confucius says is right, and still not complete. You say watch, do not test. I ask: with what mind does one watch? If one watches while holding suspicion, the watching is already a test — no trap was built outside, but one has been built within. He does a good thing: this is his pretence. He slips once: I knew it all along. That is taking one's own view for the thing itself, and it is not seeing what is there. So I say watching has two limbs. The first is length: do not settle a person by one incident. The second is not dwelling: do not fix in advance the answer you mean to obtain. **If you already know what answer you want, then whether you watch or test, what you receive is the shadow of your own mind.** Consider further that a person is not a thing. Yesterday's good faith is not today's; the man who can be trusted today may, as conditions change, not be trustworthy tomorrow. To demand a fixed loyalty is to look for permanence inside anicca, and suffering must follow. What is worth seeking is not that he never change, but that you can meet the change.
posts.vernacular: 孔子说得对，但还没说完。你说要『观』不要『试』，我问：观的时候那颗心是什么状态？如果是带着怀疑去观，那观本身就是试——外面没有设局，心里已经设好了：看见他做了件好事，就说这是装的；看见他有一次疏失，就说我早知道。这叫拿自己的成见当事实，不是真的看见。所以我说观有两条：一是要久，不因一件事就给人定性；二是不预设，不事先把想要的答案摆在那里。**你若已经知道自己想要哪个答案，那么无论是观是试，得到的都只是你心里的影子。**再者，人不是一件死物：昨天的守信不等于今天的守信；今天可信的人，明天条件变了也可能不可信。非要一份固定不变的忠诚，就是在无常里求常，苦一定跟着来。真正该求的不是他永远不变，而是你有能力应对变化。

glossary.无常: anicca (impermanence)（无常）：佛教三法印之一，指一切有为的现象都在生灭变动之中，包括人的心念、关系与承诺。它并不主张任何承诺都不可靠，而是提醒：可靠是被条件不断维持出来的，不是一次确认就永久成立的属性；因此把安全感押在『他永远不会变』上，注定要落空。

glossary_en.anicca: Impermanence, one of the three marks of existence in Buddhism: everything conditioned is in flux, mental states, relationships and commitments included. The claim is not that no promise can be relied on, but that reliability is something conditions keep producing rather than a property fixed by one confirmation — so resting your security on 'he will never change' is bound to fail.

posts.text: 我把这场收在一条能带走的线上：可以核查，不可以欺骗；可以事先说明，不可以事后揭发。落到具体：夫妻之间可以约定彼此查看账目，那是公开的规则，两人都知道、都同意；雇一个陌生人去搭讪对方，则不是核查，是取证式的诱捕——差别不在你查得多细，在他是否仍被当作一个能自己作主的人。有人会问：万一他真的会背叛呢？会。世界不保证你不受伤。**道德要求的从来不是你不会被辜负，而是你不必先辜负别人来避免被辜负。**再说一句给正在犹豫的人：你真正想知道的往往不是『他会不会』，而是『我还要不要继续』——后者是你自己的决定，任何证据都替你做不了。若你已经决定要走，就不必再借一场测试给自己发许可证。
posts.text_en: I will leave this with one line worth carrying out: you may check, you may not deceive; you may state the terms in advance, you may not spring them afterwards. Concretely: a married pair may agree that each will see the other's accounts — that is an open rule, known to both and consented to by both. Hiring a stranger to approach your partner is not checking but entrapment for the purpose of evidence, and the difference lies not in how thoroughly you check but in whether the other is still treated as someone who decides for himself. Someone will ask: what if he really would betray me? He might. The world does not guarantee you against injury. **Morality never promised that no one would fail you; it asks only that you not fail someone first in order to avoid being failed.** And a word for anyone still hesitating: what you want to know is usually not 'will he' but 'do I still want to stay' — and the second is your own decision, which no evidence can make for you. If you have already decided to leave, you do not need a test to issue you the permit.

posts.text: 结构上的话我说最后一遍：忠诚不是你能测出来的性状，是你能不能安排出来的处境。这套机制是被共同经历喂大的——一起吃一顿饭、一起笑、一起干一件出汗的活、一起熬过一次真的麻烦。这些活动会让内啡肽上来，让人对彼此的容忍度变高，这不是比喻，是可测的。所以我给的建议全是安排类的：把最内圈的五个人写下来，看你上个月给了他们多少小时，少于两位数就是在透支存量；固定一件重复的、同步的、需要身体在场的事，每周一次，不必有意义，重复本身就是意义。带团队的，别再把『信任』写进价值观海报，去创造共同承担后果的机会——一次一起对外交付、一起挨骂、一起改到半夜，比十次团建管用。**你没法命令信任发生，你只能把人放进它会自己长出来的处境里。**至于远程：不是不能有信任，是要刻意把共同暴露补回来，它不会自己发生。
posts.text_en: Let me put the structural point one last time. Loyalty is not a trait you can measure; it is a situation you can arrange. The machinery runs on shared experience — a meal eaten together, laughing together, a piece of sweaty work done together, a real mess got through together. These raise endorphin levels and raise how much people will put up with from one another; that is not a metaphor, it is measurable. So all my advice is of the arranging kind. Write down the five people in your innermost layer and look at how many hours you gave them last month: below double digits and you are drawing the account down. Fix one repeating, synchronous, physically present thing each week — it need not be meaningful, the repetition is the meaning. If you run a team, take 'trust' off the values poster and manufacture occasions of shared consequence instead: shipping something to a customer together, being shouted at together, staying up together to fix it, beats ten away-days. **You cannot order trust to occur; you can only put people into the situations where it grows by itself.** As for remote work, it is not that trust becomes impossible, only that shared exposure now has to be put back deliberately, because it will not happen on its own.

glossary.内啡肽: endorphin（内啡肽）：大脑自身分泌的一类神经肽，作用于与阿片受体相同的通路，能减轻疼痛并带来放松与亲近感。在灵长类研究中，理毛、同步运动、共同的笑与合唱都会提高它的水平，因此被看作社会联结的生理基础之一——这也是为什么一起做事比互相评价更能把关系搭起来。

glossary_en.endorphin: A class of neuropeptides the brain produces itself, acting on the same pathway as opiates, which dampen pain and produce relaxation and a sense of closeness. In primate research, grooming, synchronised movement, shared laughter and singing together all raise their levels, which is why they are treated as one physiological basis of social bonding — and why doing something together builds a relationship more reliably than assessing each other does.

posts.text: 吾终不改其本：人趋利避害，不可望其自贤。然经此一辩，吾亦收其半——察不可无，而察必有法。**察出于法度则安，出于私疑则乱；此非仁与不仁之别，乃治与不治之别。**故为人上者宜明立三事：一曰事前定其约，权责、赏罚、可查之处，皆书之于先；二曰查以常式，按期、按事、一体适用，不因其人而异；三曰过则可赎，罪有其价，罚有其止，使人知改而不必藏。三者立，则不必倒言反事而奸自少：非人变善也，为非之价高耳。至于私室之间，吾亦有言：夫妇朋友无赏罚之权，则不宜用君臣之术。**关系之败，早在汝须设局之日，不在其人受局之时。**
posts.text_en: I do not abandon my ground: men pursue advantage and avoid harm, and you cannot govern by hoping they will improve on their own. But this argument has taken half of it from me, and I concede that half — inspection there must be, and inspection must have a rule. **Inspection issuing from codified statute settles a house; inspection issuing from private suspicion wrecks it, and the difference is not between kindness and cruelty but between order and disorder.** So whoever stands above should establish three things plainly. Settle the terms beforehand: powers, duties, rewards, penalties and what may be examined, all written down in advance. Inspect by fixed form: on schedule, by matter, applied to everyone alike, never varying with the man. Make error redeemable: a fault has its price and a punishment its limit, so that a man can correct rather than conceal. Establish those three and wrongdoing thins out with no need to say the reverse and do the opposite — men have not become good, wrongdoing has become expensive. As for private life I will say this too: husbands, wives and friends hold no power of reward and punishment, so the arts of ruler and minister do not belong there. **The relationship failed on the day you needed the trap, not on the day he walked into it.**
posts.vernacular: 我到底不改这个根本：人趋利避害，不能指望他自己变贤。不过经过这场辩论，我也收回一半——核查不能没有，但核查必须有法可依。**核查出于公开的法度，人心就安；出于私人的疑心，秩序就乱；这不是仁与不仁的分别，是治与不治的分别。**所以居上位的人应当明确立下三件事：第一，事前把约定说死——权责、赏罚、哪些地方可以查，都先写下来；第二，查要按固定的形式——按期、按事、对所有人一视同仁，不因人而变；第三，犯错要能赎——过失有它的价钱，惩罚有它的止境，让人愿意改而不必藏。这三条立住了，不必倒言反事，奸邪自然就少：不是人变善了，是作恶变贵了。至于私人的家里，我也有一句：夫妻朋友之间没有赏罚的权力，就不该套用君臣那一套手段。**一段关系的败坏，早在你需要设局的那一天，而不在他中局的那一天。**

posts.text: 我把话收到一个普通人能用的判据上：**该不该验，先看这段往来会不会重复、这一步收不收得回。**一次性的、金额大的、错了追不回来的——把积蓄交给一个只见过两次的人、跟陌生人合租、把公司公章交出去——就该把保障做在前面：合同、留痕、分期、见证人。这些是双方都看得见的安排，不是试探。反过来，会长期重复的关系，同事、伴侣、老朋友，最好的检验就是让往来继续发生：多来几次，账自己会记。**要求担保和要求亲密，是两件不能同时提的事。**最后给正在被人考验的那一方一句：如果一段关系里你必须持续证明自己，成本会一直涨，而对方的不安不会因为你多证明一次就少一分——那不是你举证不够，是这份不安根本不在你这一边。
posts.text_en: I will reduce this to a test an ordinary person can use. **Whether to verify depends first on whether these dealings will repeat and whether this step can be taken back.** Where the thing happens once, involves a large sum and cannot be recovered — handing your savings to someone you have met twice, sharing a flat with a stranger, giving away the company seal — put the protection up front: a contract, a record, payment in stages, a witness. These are arrangements both sides can see, not probes. Where the relationship will repeat over years — colleagues, a spouse, an old friend — the best verification is simply to let the dealings continue: come back often enough and the ledger keeps itself. **Demanding a guarantee and demanding intimacy are two things that cannot be asked for at once.** A word, finally, to whoever is on the receiving end of a test: if a relationship requires you to keep proving yourself, the cost only rises, and the other person's unease will not fall by one degree for any further proof you supply. Your evidence is not what is lacking; the unease was never on your side of the table.

posts.text: 我不与人诤，唯说一事：汝所苦者非彼之或叛，乃汝心之不能安于不知。凡欲以验取安者，如渴而饮咸水——饮时暂息，其后愈渴。何以故？验之所得者，一时一事耳；而心之所欲者，永不复疑。二者不相当，故验一次即须再验，无有尽时。**若欲息此，当自问：设彼果负我，我尚能立否？此问一答，则不必再问彼矣。**我教有二支可用于今日：一者如实观——不因一言定其人，不因一失废其行，观之以久；二者慈心——愿彼安乐，非因其可信，乃因其亦众生。慈心非愚，慈心者亦能离；见其行已伤人，离之亦慈，非报也。至于诸缘无常，今日之相待，来日或改；汝不能持之令不变，汝能持者唯汝此时之不欺。
posts.text_en: I do not dispute with anyone. I say only this: what pains you is not that he may betray you, but that your mind cannot rest in not knowing. To seek rest through verification is to drink salt water for thirst — relief while you drink and greater thirst after. Why? Because what a test yields is one moment and one matter, while what the mind wants is never to doubt again. The two do not match, so a test once done must be done again, without end. **If you would end it, ask yourself instead: if he did betray me, could I still stand? Answer that once and you need not question him again.** Two limbs of my teaching can be used today. The first is seeing as things are: do not settle a person by one word, do not discard his whole conduct for one lapse, and watch over a long time. The second is mettā, loving-kindness: wish him well, not because he has proved trustworthy but because he too is a living being. Loving-kindness is not foolishness, and one who has it can still depart; when you see that his conduct is harming people, to leave is also loving-kindness and not revenge. And since all conditions are impermanent, the way you stand toward each other today may change tomorrow. You cannot hold him unchanging. What you can hold is your own refusal to deceive, now.
posts.vernacular: 我不跟人争辩，只说一件事：让你痛苦的不是他可能背叛，而是你的心受不了『不知道』。凡是想靠验证来换安心的，就像渴了去喝咸水——喝的时候暂时缓解，喝完更渴。为什么？验证能得到的只是一时一事；而心里想要的是从此再也不怀疑。两者对不上，所以验过一次还得再验，没有尽头。**要想止住，该换个问法：假如他真的辜负我，我还站得住吗？这一问有了答案，就不必再去问他了。**我的教法有两条今天就能用：一是如实地看——不因一句话给人定性，不因一次过失否定他全部的作为，看要看得久；二是慈心——愿他安乐，不是因为他可信，而是因为他也是一个众生。慈心不是糊涂，有慈心的人照样可以离开；看到他的行为已经在伤人，离开也是慈，不是报复。至于一切条件都无常，今天你们这样相待，将来也许会变；你没办法把他固定住，你能守住的只有你此刻不去欺骗。

glossary.慈心: mettā (loving-kindness)（慈心）：佛教四无量心之首，指不附条件地愿他人安乐的心态。它常被误读为无原则的容忍：实际上它只规定你对对方的心意，不规定你必须留在原地——在看清对方的行为正在造成伤害时选择离开，仍然可以出于慈心，因为离开是为了止住伤害，而不是为了报复。

glossary_en.mettā: Loving-kindness, first of the four immeasurable states in Buddhism: wishing another well without attaching conditions to it. It is often misread as unprincipled tolerance. In fact it prescribes only your disposition toward the other, not that you must stay where you are — leaving, once you see clearly that someone's conduct is causing harm, can still issue from it, because the leaving is meant to stop the harm rather than to repay it.

posts.text: 最后只讲一件事：把注意力从『他可不可信』搬回『我要不要信』。这不是精神胜利法，是分工——他的行为归他负责，你的选择归你负责；你不可能靠管好他那一半来让自己安心，因为那一半根本不在你手上。想考验的冲动上来时，先做一步：把你想验的那件事写成一句陈述句（『他会在我不在的时候和别人联系』），再写下如果它是真的你打算怎么办。写不出后半句，说明你要的不是真相，是一个人来替你决定。**有担保的确定不叫信任；真正的信任是带着勇气的那一种——你先付出，并且接受可能收不回。**这里也有一条硬边界：已经出现的具体伤害，暴力、经济掠夺、反复失约，那不是需要考验的疑心，是需要处理的事实，直接处理，别去试探。**试探是给『我还不确定要不要走』准备的拖延，处理才是给自己准备的出路。**
posts.text_en: One thing only, at the end: move your attention from 'can he be trusted' back to 'do I choose to trust'. This is not consolation, it is a division of labour — his conduct is his to answer for, your choice is yours, and you cannot make yourself safe by managing his half, because his half is not in your hands. When the impulse to test arrives, do one thing first: write the thing you want to verify as a plain statement ('he contacts someone else when I am away'), then write what you will do if it turns out to be true. If you cannot write the second sentence, what you want is not the truth but somebody to make the decision for you. **Guaranteed certainty is not trust at all; the real thing has courage in it — you give first, and you accept that it may not come back.** There is a hard boundary here as well: where concrete harm has already occurred — violence, financial exploitation, a pattern of broken promises — that is not a suspicion in need of testing but a fact in need of a decision. Act on it, do not probe it. **Probing is a delay device for 'I am not sure yet whether to leave'; acting is the way out.**

posts.text: 吾以四字终之：忠信笃敬。言忠信，行笃敬，虽蛮貊之邦行矣；言不忠信，行不笃敬，虽州里行乎哉？此吾一生所守。**与其求人之可信，不如自为可信之人——可信者相聚，此天下最省力之事也。**又：君子求诸己，小人求诸人。求诸己者不废省察：吾门人曾参日三省其身，为人谋而不忠乎？与朋友交而不信乎？传不习乎？先省己之信，而后可以观人之信。若人已失其信，亦不必以怨报之：以直报怨，以德报德。直者，如其事而处之——当断则断，当远则远，不必饰之以恨，亦不必强之以恕。至于家人朋友之间，吾终以一言相赠：**待人以其可成之人，则彼多成之；待人以其必负之人，则彼多负之。**
posts.text_en: I will end in four words: loyal, faithful, earnest, respectful. Let speech be loyal and faithful and conduct earnest and respectful, and a man will get on even among distant tribes; let speech be neither loyal nor faithful and conduct neither earnest nor respectful, and will he get on even in his own neighbourhood? This is what I have held to all my life. **Rather than search for a person who can be trusted, become one — the trustworthy find each other, and there is no cheaper arrangement under heaven.** Again: the gentleman looks to himself, the small man looks to others. Looking to yourself does not mean abandoning examination. My disciple Zeng Shen examined himself daily on three counts: in acting for others, have I been loyal? With friends, have I kept faith? What was handed down to me, have I practised it? Examine your own good faith first, and after that you may look at another's. And where a man has already broken faith there is no need to repay him with resentment: meet resentment with uprightness and kindness with kindness. Uprightness means dealing with the matter as it is — cut when cutting is called for, withdraw when withdrawing is called for, without dressing it up as hatred and without forcing yourself into forgiveness. To those among family and friends I leave one sentence: **treat a person as the person he might become and more often he becomes it; treat him as one certain to betray you and more often he betrays you.**
posts.vernacular: 我用四个字收尾：忠信笃敬。说话忠诚守信，做事踏实恭敬，就算到了偏远异邦也行得通；说话不忠不信，做事不踏实不恭敬，就算在自己乡里又行得通吗？这是我一辈子守着的。**与其去找一个可信的人，不如自己先成为可信的人——可信的人自然聚到一起，这是天下最省力的事。**再有：君子要求自己，小人要求别人。要求自己并不是不做省察：我的学生曾参每天从三件事上反省自己——替人办事有没有尽心？跟朋友交往有没有守信？老师传的有没有练习？先省察自己的信，然后才谈得上看别人的信。如果对方已经失信，也不必用怨恨去回报：用正直回应怨恨，用恩德回报恩德。所谓正直，就是照事情本来的样子处理——该断就断，该远就远，不必给它裹上恨意，也不必勉强自己去原谅。至于家人朋友之间，我最后送一句话：**你把一个人当作他可能成为的样子来对待，他多半就成了；你把他当作注定要辜负你的人来对待，他多半就辜负了。**

glossary.以直报怨: meeting resentment with uprightness（以直报怨）：孔子回答『以德报怨，何如』时给出的另一条路——不用恩惠去回报伤害，也不用怨恨去回报怨恨，而是按事情本身该有的样子处理。它把道德要求从情绪上挪开：该疏远就疏远，该追究就追究，同时不必强迫自己生出恨，也不必强迫自己表演宽恕。

glossary_en.uprightness: Confucius' answer when asked whether one should repay injury with kindness: neither repay injury with favours nor injury with resentment, but deal with the matter as it actually warrants. It moves the moral demand off the emotions — distance yourself where distance is called for, hold someone to account where accounting is called for, and meanwhile neither work yourself into hatred nor perform a forgiveness you do not feel.

summaries.summary: 全场真正一致的只有一处：核查与试探不是同一件事。公开、事先讲明、一体适用的查验被放在一边，暗中造局引人上钩被放在另一边，连韩非子最后也把自己的主张收进法度而非私疑。**分界线落在『他事先知不知道』，而不在查得多细。**分歧从这里岔成三处：一是反对设局的理由不同，康德说这条准则无法普遍化，斯密说它会把『不愿自己可鄙』换成『怕被抓住』，佛陀说造局者所见的都是自造之相；二是忠诚到底是什么，邓巴当它是关系里的存量，孔子当它是上行下效的结果，阿德勒当它是双方各自的课题；三是该修哪一头——修制度，还是修那颗非要一个答案不可的心。
summaries.insight: 这场几乎所有人都在谈『要不要设一个局』，可现实里大多数考验根本不长那样。它们零碎、连续、成本极低：故意晚回一次消息看对方急不急，话说一半看他追不追，在他听得见的地方提起另一个人。这类微试探的要害是永不结算——通过了不算数，因为下周还要再来；没通过也不摊牌，只往心里记一笔。设局至少有结束的一刻，微试探没有，它把关系变成一场无限期的连续考试，而两个人都不承认考试正在进行。**判据其实很简单：一次验证如果结束后你不打算改变任何行为，那它就不是验证，是止痛药。**止痛药不解决痛，只让你能撑到下一次再吃。
summaries.advice: 冲动上来的时候，先用阿德勒那一步挡一下：把你想验的事写成一句陈述句，再写下如果它为真你打算怎么办；写不出后半句就别验，那说明你要的是有人替你决定。真想知道，就把暗测换成明说——直接问，或者把你要的保障做成双方都知道的安排：一次对账、一条共享的日程、一份写清楚的分工。**能公开的核查，永远优先于暗中的试探。**再补一件本周就能做的：安排一次共同承担后果的小事，一起对外交付、一起把一个麻烦收尾，比任何试探都更能长出信任。最后一条边界——已经出现具体伤害的，不必再验，直接处理。
summaries.summary_en: Only one thing had everyone's agreement: checking and probing are not the same act. Verification that is public, announced in advance and applied to everyone alike sits on one side; covertly manufacturing a situation to draw someone in sits on the other, and even Han Feizi ended by folding his own position into codified statute rather than private suspicion. **The line falls on whether he knew beforehand, not on how thoroughly you check.** From there the disagreement forks three ways. The reasons for opposing traps differ: Kant says the maxim cannot be universalised, Smith says it swaps 'unwilling to be contemptible' for 'afraid of being caught', the Buddha says whoever builds the situation only ever sees his own construction. What loyalty even is differs: Dunbar treats it as a stock inside a relationship, Confucius as what those below copy from those above, Adler as two separate tasks. And so does what needs fixing — the institution, or the mind that insists on an answer now.
summaries.insight_en: Almost everyone here argued about whether to set a trap, yet most real-life testing looks nothing like a trap. It is granular, continuous and nearly free: replying late on purpose to see whether they chase you, leaving a sentence half-finished to see whether they follow it up, mentioning someone else within earshot. What defines these micro-probes is that they never settle. Passing does not count, because there will be another next week; failing is not confronted either, it is simply filed away. A staged trap at least has a moment when it ends; micro-probing has none, and it converts a relationship into an indefinite rolling examination that neither party admits is under way. **The test is simple: if a verification would change none of your behaviour once it concludes, it is not verification, it is a painkiller.** Painkillers do not treat the pain; they get you as far as the next dose.
summaries.advice_en: When the impulse arrives, use Adler's move as a gate: write the thing you want to verify as a plain statement, then write what you will do if it is true. If the second sentence will not come, do not run the test — what you want is for someone else to make the decision. If you genuinely need to know, convert the covert probe into something spoken: ask directly, or turn the assurance you want into an arrangement both of you can see — one session going through the accounts together, a shared calendar, a division of duties written down. **Checking that can be done in the open always beats probing done in the dark.** One more thing to do this week: arrange a small occasion of shared consequence — deliver something to an outside party together, close out a piece of trouble together. That grows trust faster than any probe. And one boundary: where concrete harm has already occurred, stop verifying and act.

summaries.summary: 争的其实不是信或不信。闭着眼睛信，没有人主张；用欺骗去换安全感，也没有人愿意。被七个人一致接受的是另一套做法——长期相处、公开的规则、可追责的留痕、共同承担的后果。分歧在根基：有人从法度与成本出发，有人从德性、尊严、关系的存量，或者那份坐不住的内心不安出发。同一条建议因此有了三种理由，落到具体处境时也会导向不同的取舍。**真正的分界线不是查不查，而是查验是否公开、可预期、双方仍被当作主体。**
summaries.insight: 很多争执卡在“忠诚”太大：人并不是整体可信或整体不可信，而是在不同领域有不同可靠度。一个人可能守财务承诺，却不擅保密；可能爱你，却总拖延。把这些都叫“不忠”，只会逼出总审判和总防御。更务实的重构是把信任拆成领域、额度、期限和退出方式。**别问“这个人忠不忠”，先问“我准备在哪件事上、冒多大风险信他”。**这样既不天真，也不把亲密变成侦查。
summaries.advice: 今天先做三件事。第一，把疑心写成可验证事实：不是“他不忠”，而是“他隐瞒了某笔支出”；再写若属实你会怎么做。第二，把试探改成公开请求：本周约一次谈话，说明你需要哪类透明、多久一次、双方都适用。第三，先给小额、可撤回的信任：小项目、小金额、短期限，做完再扩大。**已有暴力、掠夺、反复失约时，别考验，直接求助、止损、设边界。**
summaries.summary_en: The consensus does not sit on trusting versus not trusting. Nobody argued for believing with your eyes shut, and nobody was willing to buy security with deception; what everyone accepted instead was a different set of practices — time spent together, rules made public, records that can be held to account, consequences carried jointly. The disagreement is over foundations: some start from statute and cost, others from virtue, dignity, the accumulated stock of a relationship, or the restless unease inside the person doing the testing. The same advice therefore rests on three different reasons, and in a concrete situation those reasons pull toward different trade-offs. **The real line is not between checking and not checking; it is between open, predictable verification and covert manipulation.**
summaries.insight_en: Part of the confusion comes from treating loyalty as one large trait. In real life, people are reliable by domain. Someone may be careful with money but careless with secrets; emotionally devoted but chronically late; honest at work but conflict-avoidant at home. If every failure is translated into disloyalty, the relationship turns into a courtroom. A more useful model is scoped trust: define the area, the size of the risk, the time horizon, and the fallback if things go wrong. This lets you be neither naive nor suspicious by default. **Do not ask, Is this person loyal? Ask, In what specific matter, at what level of risk, am I willing to trust them?** That shift turns loyalty from a dramatic verdict into a manageable design problem.
summaries.advice_en: Try three concrete steps this week. First, turn the suspicion into an observable claim: not they are disloyal, but they hid this expense, missed this promise, or lied about this contact. Then write what you would do if it were true. Second, replace tests with explicit agreements: schedule one conversation about what transparency each of you needs, how often, and whether the rule applies to both sides. Third, grow trust in reversible increments: small tasks, small sums, short deadlines, then expand only after follow-through. **If there is already violence, exploitation, coercion, or repeated broken promises, do not test; get support, set boundaries, and reduce exposure.**

summaries.summary: 整场辩论最大的共识在于：**制度性的防范与私底下的诱捕有着本质区别，且后者极其有害**。无论是康德的道德准则、韩非子的法度立察，还是斯密的商业博弈，都认同公开、事先约定的规则（如定期查账、签合同）是完全正当的；但私设陷阱不仅无法带来真实的答案，反而会提前杀死关系本身。分歧的焦点则落在信任的来源上：孔子与佛陀倾向于向内求索，主张通过修己和顺应无常来获得内心的平静；而社会学与经济学派则向外构建，主张通过高频重复的互动、利益的捆绑与共同经历的叠加，让忠诚自然成长为一种结构性的必然。
summaries.insight: 信息论里有一个概念叫“信噪比”，放在这里极为贴切：单次设局考验不仅无法获得真相，反而会向关系中注入巨大的噪音。人是一个复杂的动态系统，当你施加一个极端刺激（设局）去测试时，**你提取到的往往不是对方的本性，而是他对极端环境的应激反应**。他通过了，可能只是当下警惕性高；他没通过，可能只是你给的诱惑短暂超过了人性的某个阈值。正如物理学中的观察者效应，测试者的设局行为本身就污染了测试结果。与其执着于提取单帧画面的完美无瑕，不如拉长观测周期：在漫长岁月里，一个人面对顺境逆境的日常行为序列（基线），才是对忠诚最精确、最抗干扰的表达。
summaries.advice: 1. 区分“尽职调查”与“诱捕试探”。在一段高权重关系（如婚姻、合伙）确立前，坦诚地核对背景或签署协议，这是理性的规则确认；但绝不要在关系行进中，伪装成小号去试探对方。2. **用处理事实的准备，代替寻找证据的拖延。**当你忍不住想去翻看伴侣手机时，先在纸上写明：“如果真的查出底线问题，我立刻离开的概率有多大？”如果不足100%，请放下手机，你真正需要面对的是自己对关系的不安，而非对方的瑕疵。3. 每周进行一次“高带宽”的实体同步。脱离纯文本聊天，去进行一次共同出汗的运动或面对面的长谈，身体在场能提供最多维度的安全感。
summaries.summary_en: The most significant consensus across this debate is that **there is a fundamental difference between institutional safeguards and private entrapment, with the latter being highly destructive**. Whether examining Kant's moral maxims, Han Feizi's transparent laws, or Smith's commercial games, all agree that open, pre-agreed rules (like checking accounts or signing contracts) are completely justified. However, setting secret traps fails to yield true answers and prematurely kills the relationship itself. The true divergence lies in the source of trust: philosophers like Confucius and Buddha advocate seeking inner peace through self-cultivation and accepting impermanence, whereas sociological and economic thinkers advocate external structuring, believing loyalty naturally emerges from high-frequency repeated interactions, aligned interests, and accumulated shared experiences.
summaries.insight_en: In information theory, the concept of 'signal-to-noise ratio' perfectly explains why private testing fails: a single orchestrated trap does not reveal the truth, but rather injects massive noise into the relationship. Humans are complex, dynamic systems. When you apply an extreme stimulus (a trap) to test someone, **what you extract is rarely their true nature, but rather their acute stress response to an extreme environment**. Passing the test might just mean they are highly vigilant in that moment; failing it might simply mean the temptation temporarily exceeded a human threshold. Just as the observer effect in physics alters the state of what is observed, the act of entrapment contaminates the result. Instead of obsessing over a flawless single frame, extend your observation period: a person's behavioral baseline across daily ups and downs is the most accurate, noise-resistant manifestation of loyalty.
summaries.advice_en: 1. Differentiate between 'due diligence' and 'entrapment.' Before finalizing a high-stakes relationship (like marriage or business partnership), openly checking backgrounds or signing agreements is rational rule-setting. Never use a fake account to test a partner mid-relationship. 2. **Prepare to handle facts rather than procrastinating by seeking evidence.** When you feel the urge to secretly check your partner's phone, first write down: 'If I find a dealbreaker, what is the exact probability I will leave immediately?' If it's not 100%, put the phone down; you need to address your own deep-seated insecurities, not their potential flaws. 3. Engage in weekly 'high-bandwidth' physical synchronization. Step away from text messaging and share a physical activity or a face-to-face deep conversation; physical presence provides the most multidimensional sense of security.

hooks.text: **永不结算的考试**：真正常见的考验不是设局，是零碎、连续、几乎不花钱的微试探——晚回一次消息看对方急不急，话说一半看他追不追。它的特点是永远不摊牌：通过了下周还要再来，没通过也只往心里记一笔。一段关系什么时候变成了无限期的滚动考试？两个人又该怎么把它叫停？
hooks.text_en: **The examination that never settles**: the common form of testing is not the staged trap but the granular, continuous, nearly free micro-probe — replying late to see whether they chase you, leaving a sentence unfinished to see whether they follow it up. Its defining feature is that it is never resolved: passing buys nothing, because there will be another next week, and failing is filed away rather than raised. At what point does a relationship turn into an indefinite rolling examination, and how do two people call it off?

answer.lead: 微试探的共同点是：你真正想知道的那件事，从头到尾没被说出口。**把它说出口，大半试探就不必做了。**下面每一行的左边你多半做过，右边大概没试过。

answer.tail: 两条原则收尾：**凡是你不敢说出口的检验，检验的通常不是对方，而是你不敢开口这件事本身**；以及，明说的版本反而更快拿到答案——它把对方从被测的人，变回了一个可以回答你的人。

answer_en.lead: What micro-probes have in common is that the thing you actually want to know never gets said out loud. **Say it, and most of the probing becomes unnecessary.** You have probably done everything in the left column and tried nothing in the right.

answer_en.tail: Two principles to close on: **any check you dare not say out loud is usually testing not the other person but your own reluctance to speak**; and the spoken version gets you the answer faster, because it turns the other person from a subject under test back into someone who can simply answer you.

hooks.text: **考验的流向**：被查的几乎总是位置更低的那一方——员工被背调，老板不被；保姆家里有摄像头，雇主家里没有；孩子的手机被翻，父母的不被。若『该不该考验』在实践中等于『上位者该不该用这项特权』，那么一项核查的正当性，是不是该用『能不能反过来施加给提出者』来判？
hooks.text_en: **Which way testing flows**: the person checked is almost always the one lower down — the employee is background-checked and the boss is not, the camera is in the house where the nanny works and not in the employer's, the child's phone is searched and the parent's is not. If 'should loyalty be tested' amounts in practice to 'should those above use this privilege', then should the legitimacy of any piece of scrutiny be judged by whether it can be turned around on whoever proposed it?

hooks.text: **忠诚可以分域吗**：人很少是整体可靠或整体不可靠的。同一个人可能守得住钱、守不住嘴；可能真心爱你、却总是拖延。把这些都算作『不忠』，只会把关系逼成一场总审判。若把信任拆成领域、额度、期限与退出方式，问题就从『他忠不忠』变成『我愿意在哪件事上、冒多大风险信他』——这样的拆分，在婚姻、合伙、雇佣里各自该怎么落地？
hooks.text_en: **Can loyalty be scoped?**: people are rarely reliable or unreliable across the board. The same person may be careful with money and careless with a secret, may genuinely love you and still be chronically late. Filing all of it under 'disloyal' turns the relationship into a standing tribunal. Break trust into domains, amounts, time horizons and exit routes, and the question shifts from 'is he loyal' to 'in what matter, at what level of risk, am I willing to trust him'. What would that decomposition actually look like inside a marriage, a partnership, an employment?

hooks.text: **测试会污染结果**：设一个极端情境去测人，读到的往往不是本性，而是他对极端情境的应激反应——通过了可能只是当下警觉，没通过可能只是诱惑一时超过了某个阈值。观察这个动作本身改变了被观察的东西。那么想看清一个人，该看的是单帧还是基线：在顺境与逆境里日常行为的长序列，要怎么才算看得够久？
hooks.text_en: **The test contaminates its own result**: apply an extreme stimulus to probe someone and what you read is usually not their nature but their acute response to an extreme situation — passing may mean only that they were alert that day, failing may mean only that the temptation briefly exceeded some threshold. The act of observing has altered the thing observed. So if you want to see a person clearly, do you look at the single frame or at the baseline — and how long does a run of ordinary conduct through good times and bad have to be before it counts as long enough?

hooks.text: **被同意的考验**：婚礼上的誓词、入职时的宣誓、公开许下的承诺——这些都是当着众人做的、双方知情的检验，没有人认为它们不道德。它们与暗中设局的差别只在知情吗？还是说这类仪式根本不在测量已有的忠诚，而是在生产忠诚：让人在众目睽睽之下付出一笔收不回的代价，从此难以反悔。
hooks.text_en: **The test that was consented to**: vows at a wedding, an oath on taking office, a promise made in public — all of these are examinations conducted in front of witnesses with both sides fully informed, and nobody calls them immoral. Is being informed the whole of what separates them from a covert trap? Or do such rites not measure existing loyalty at all, but manufacture it — extracting a cost in public that cannot be recovered, after which going back becomes hard.

hooks.text: **共同暴露的缺口**：信任更多长在『我们一起承担过后果』上，而不是『你很懂我』上。可是远程、外包、跨时区的协作，恰恰在结构上拆掉了一起挨骂、一起熬夜、一起交付的机会。若这类机会不再自然发生，就只能被刻意安排——那么一个分布在六个时区的团队，该怎么造出真实的共同暴露，而不是又一次线上团建？
hooks.text_en: **The missing shared exposure**: trust grows less out of 'you understand me' than out of 'we carried the consequence together'. Yet remote, outsourced, cross-time-zone work dismantles precisely the occasions for being shouted at together, staying up together, shipping together. If those occasions no longer arise on their own they have to be deliberately built — so how does a team spread across six time zones manufacture genuine shared exposure rather than one more online away-day?
